title: A finite-type birational monomorphism to a normal Noetherian scheme is open
statement: Let $f:X\to Z$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Assume $Z$ is Noetherian, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact, and normal, meaning that every local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Assume $X$ is reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Suppose $f$ is a monomorphism: for every scheme $T$, the map $\operatorname{Hom}(T,X)\to\operatorname{Hom}(T,Z)$ induced by $f$ is injective. Suppose there is a dense open subscheme $H\subseteq Z$ such that $f^{-1}(H)$ is dense in $X$ and $f:f^{-1}(H)\to H$ is an isomorphism. Then $f$ is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion]. No flatness of $f$, irreducibility of $Z$, or properness is assumed.

source.place: Tag 02LR, lemma-quasi-finite-separated-quasi-affine, normal-target consequence; morphisms.tex Tag 0CT8, lemma-monomorphism-loc-finite-type-loc-quasi-finite, and Tag 0AB1, lemma-finite-birational-over-normal. Bosch–Lütkebohmert–Raynaud, Néron Models, 2.3 Theorem 2′ (Zariski's Main Theorem, weak form), printed p.46 (PDF p.53), as used in 5.3 Lemma 3, printed p.121.

proof.text: By clause (2) of [rem-pc-regular-normal], write $Z=\coprod_i Z_i$ as a finite disjoint union of normal integral open subschemes. Both hypotheses of that clause hold: $Z$ is Noetherian and all its local rings are normal domains. The $Z_i$ cover $Z$; no choice of a component is needed when $Z$ is empty. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-opens-basis], cover each $Z_i$ by nonempty affine opens $V$. Each such $V$ is also open and affine in $Z$. We prove that $f_V:f^{-1}(V)\to V$ is an open immersion for each $V$.

Fix one such $V$, put $W=f^{-1}(V)$ and $H_V=H\cap V$. The open $V$ of integral $Z_i$ is nonempty and irreducible and has the same local rings there, hence is integral and normal. Density of $H$ makes $H_V$ nonempty; an open subset of an irreducible space is irreducible if nonempty. The given isomorphism identifies $f^{-1}(H_V)$ with $H_V$. Since $W$ is open in $X$, density of $f^{-1}(H)$ in $X$ makes $f^{-1}(H_V)=W\cap f^{-1}(H)$ dense in $W$. The closure of an irreducible subspace is irreducible: two relatively open sets meeting its closure both meet the subspace and therefore meet each other. Thus $W$ is nonempty and irreducible. Its local rings are those of reduced $X$, so it is reduced by [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Consequently $W$ and $V$ are integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme].

source.place: Tags 01OK and 01ON, definition-integral and lemma-characterize-integral; elementary open-subspace argument

proof.text: The affine-cover definition [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] shows that $f_V$ is of finite type: an affine open of $V$ is an affine open of $Z$, with the same inverse image in $X$ and in $W$. It is a monomorphism, since two maps to $W$ equal after $f_V$ are equal as maps to $X$ by the hypothesis on $f$, and maps to an open subscheme are determined by their maps to $X$. Apply [lem-trf-monomorphism-finite-type-composite-lqf] with $g=\mathrm{id}_V$. It gives separatedness and unramifiedness of $f_V$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-fibre-point-isolated] at each point of $W$, taking the unramified neighbourhood to be all of $W$. Every point is isolated in its fibre; finite type therefore makes $f_V$ quasi-finite by [pqf-def-quasifinite].

The affine scheme $V$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Apply [pqf-lem-normalization-open] to the separated finite-type quasi-finite map $f_V$. Its relative-normalization factorization is $W\xrightarrow{j}N\xrightarrow{p}V$, with $j$ a quasi-compact open immersion, $p$ integral and $p\circ j=f_V$. Finite type gives quasi-compactness of $f_V$, and separatedness gives quasi-separatedness, since its diagonal is a closed immersion. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-relative-normalization] applies to this same relative normalization; clause (iv), using integrality of $W$ from step 2, makes $N$ integral.

source.place: Tag 02LR, lemma-quasi-finite-separated-quasi-affine; morphisms.tex Tags 035H/035I and 0AXN for the same normalization

proof.text: The nonempty integral schemes $W,N,V$ have unique generic points by [lem-sc-scheme-sober]. A generic point belongs to every nonempty open. The open immersion $j$ identifies the generic point of $W$ with that of $N$ and their local rings. Likewise the isomorphism $f^{-1}(H_V)\simeq H_V$, between nonempty opens of $W$ and $V$, identifies their generic points and local rings; these are exactly the maps induced by $f_V$. Since $p\circ j=f_V$, the generic point of $N$ maps to that of $V$ under $p$, and the induced generic local-ring map is an isomorphism. By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction], these generic local rings are their function fields. Hence $p$ induces an isomorphism $k(V)\xrightarrow{\sim}k(N)$.

Apply [lem-trf-integral-birational-normal-isomorphism] to $p:N\to V$. Its source and target are integral by steps 2 and 4, it is integral by step 4, its generic-point and function-field conditions are step 5, and all local rings of $V$ are integrally closed domains by step 2. It follows that $p$ is an isomorphism. Thus $f_V=p\circ j$ identifies $W$ with an open subscheme of $V$, so is an open immersion by [def-weil-open-immersion].

For each $V$ let $O_V\subseteq V$ be the open image just obtained. On $V\cap V\prime$, both identifications restrict the single map $f$ to $f^{-1}(V\cap V\prime)$, and their images there are $O_V\cap V\prime=V\cap O_{V\prime}$. Their inverses agree, being inverses of the same restricted isomorphism. Therefore they glue to an isomorphism $X\simeq O=\bigcup_V O_V$ over $Z$, with $O$ open in $Z$. Equivalently, the local inverse maps glue by the sheaf axiom on open subschemes. By [def-weil-open-immersion], $f$ is an open immersion. If $Z$ is empty, the existence of $f$ forces $X$ empty and the same empty gluing gives the identity of the empty scheme.
